text:
During the inflationary pressures of 2022, we created our "MORTGAS" consumer misery index that is simply a sum of the price of gas ($/gallon) and the average 30-year fixed mortgage rate.

Our MORTGAS index hit a record low in the early 2020s when mortgage rates got below 3% and prices at the pump briefly got below $2/gallon.  Those days are long gone.

Gas prices first spiked in early 2022 when Russia invaded Ukraine, then they trended lower for the next few years until they spiked again this year with the US invasion of Iran.

Mortgage rates went from 3% up to 7% during the Fed's massive tightening cycle to address runaway inflation in 2022.  They too had been trending lower over the past few years, but they've moved higher again this year since the Iran War began.

Combined, our MORTGAS index is actually at a new record high right now, eclipsing the peak seen back in October 2023.  Consumers are feeling the pain as we head into midterm elections less than a month away.

$SBUX $CMG merger offers the wrong kind of synergy.  The overlap between the two brands is unlikely to be enough to justify a takeover premium.

The Financial Times
October 9, 2026

Putting the band back together is surely a great feeling, but a dubious corporate strategy. Starbucks chief Brian Niccol has considered a merger with Chipotle, his $41bn rival — and former employer — the FT reported on Thursday. However neat the match might seem from Starbucks’ corner office, it makes little sense for shareholders.

Niccol knows Chipotle very well indeed. He ran the Mexican-themed restaurant chain for six years before decamping in 2024 to the world’s biggest coffee chain, which was then in a state of considerable disarray. Seen from afar, the two do faintly similar things, serving comestibles to customers who are in a hurry. Both have large, sometimes restive workforces.
Moreover, the ways in which they differ might seem from a distance like opportunities. Chipotle’s balance sheet is free of debt; gearing it up a little could provide low-hanging fruit. And while Starbucks has a sprawling global network, Chipotle has yet to venture outside the US, apart from a smattering of international stores.

Here's how I think about using SI (vs AI):

AI has become the umbrella term for nearly everything happening in tech today. That term caught on first. But when you consider what companies like Tesla and SpaceX are ultimately trying to achieve, I think "super intelligence" (SI) is a more accurate description of their ambitions.

At first I thought SI was a silly term to use over AI, but after thinking about it, Tesla and SpaceX are trying to create a real super intelligence, and less so an "artificial intelligence." Think about how we describe someone who's exceptionally smart. We say they're "super intelligent." Nobody says they're "artificially intelligent."

On the surface, a $SBUX takeover of $CMG makes some sense.  Brian Niccol, CEO of SBUX, was previously CEO of CMG for 6 years and was viewed às a visionary leader after guiding CMG to record growth. That said, the synergies of offering Chipotle bowls at Starbucks or potential supply chain advantages for Starbucks seem insignificant. Buying Chipotle may be $SBUX CEO Brian Niccol’s best chance of keeping his CEO job given disappointing results so far in his two years as CEO of Starbucks ($SBUX  -3% vs SPX  +42%).   I am wary when I see a company with lackluster performance trying to acquire another company on the benefits of “synergies” that are far from obvious and likely to cause distraction when $SBUX needs leadership, product innovation, and better merchandising.

zh_summary: Dalio 談長期債務週期：債務增長快於收入，最終還款壓力迫使消費與借貸收縮，週期逆轉。沒有提及個股。
ko_summary: Dalio는 장기 부채 사이클을 설명했다: 부채가 소득보다 빠르게 늘면 결국 상환 압박으로 소비와 차입이 위축되고 사이클이 역전된다. 개별 종목 언급 없음.
text:
Over long periods of time, debts tend to rise faster than incomes, creating the long-term debt cycle.

Even as people become more indebted, lenders freely extend credit because during economic booms, incomes rise, asset values soar, and the stock market thrives. People borrow more to buy financial assets, pushing prices higher and creating a bubble.

So long as incomes keep rising, the debt burden stays manageable. But this cannot continue forever. Over decades, debt burdens slowly accumulate until debt repayments grow faster than incomes. This forces people to cut back on spending, causing incomes to fall and borrowing to dry up—eventually reversing the entire cycle.

Since April, this figure has risen +3.3 percentage points, its largest 5-month increase since October 2025.

At the same time, allocation to bonds rose +0.3 percentage points, to 14.9%, remaining below its average of 15.9% since 1987.

Appetite for risk among retail investors is through the roof.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent tells Fox's @IngrahamAngle that he hopes the Fed will keep an "open mind" on rate hikes and consider the example of the 1990s and Greenspan.

What's interesting about this oft-cited analogy is that there's the 1996-97 Greenspan who resisted hiking when some of his colleagues wanted it.

But there's also the 1999-2000 Greenspan Fed that raised rates by 175 bps in 12 months (including a 50-bps hike in May 2000), which more than reversed the 75 bps in cuts that followed the LTCM meltdown in 1998.

Ingraham nods to this history: "We did have the internet boom in 2000 and bust as well, didn't we?"

A new Tesla patent application has been published publicly today for a 3D tactile touch sensor for a humanoid robot.

These sensors could allow Optimus to detect touch, pressure, and force across different parts of its hands, improving its ability to grip and manipulate objects.

The patent says: "The separator layer can comprise a dielectric or piezoresistive material. The 3D tactile sensors can conform to curved geometries and can be used for measuring surface force, touch, and pressure. For example, the 3D tactile sensors described herein can be used in fingertips, palms, end-effectors, or other portions of a robot enabling the robot to sense the world around it. The sensors may be defined using flexible or formable material, such as thermoplastic, and can support resistive or capacitive sensing.

The 3D tactile sensors described herein can be manufactured using a variety of approaches. One example approach involves defining an array of sensing elements in a substrate material using screen printing or substrate etching. Additional approaches involve the use of 3D dispensing (e.g., 3D printing) tech-niques, pad printing techniques, or electroplating tech-niques. The substrate may be formed to a target 3D geometry using thermoforming, injection molding, or compression molding, among any other suitable techniques."

This patent was originally filed in Sept 2025. Tesla may or may not end up using this technology in Optimus: https://ppubs.uspto.gov/api/pdf/downloadPdf/US-202603

text:
Since we first started measuring economies, GDP has only ever been able to grow three ways. Population growth, plus productivity growth, plus debt growth.

That equation is The Everything Code.

And it's what has left us in the mess we're in today. We have too few workers and too much debt. When productivity cant fill the gap, the only lever left is more debt... and the only way to carry that much debt is to debase the currency. That is why everything feels more expensive every year and why your savings never seem to keep up. 

Except now, for the first time in history, we have a way out.

AI and robots change the equation itself. They add workers that dont age, dont retire, get cheaper every year, and add productivity on a scale we've never seen. 

The catch is that it's now moving faster than society, politics or economics can adapt. Coherence breaks down. That is The Economic Singularity.

This is what my book, The Everything Code, charts. It starts with the framework itself, how debt and demographics got us here, moves through The Exponential Age and ends at The Economic Singularity. Everything Ive been working on for years, in one place and in order, so you can see why we have such a short window to position ourselves before the whole system changes completely.

It's out on November 3rd.

ko_summary: 젠슨 황이 Satya Nadella의 게시물(Windows의 새 장을 연 NVIDIA 협력에 감사)을 리포스트하며 양사 협력을 돌아봤다: Windows가 플랫폼 전환을 이끌어 NVIDIA에 새 산업을 만들어 줬고, DirectX를 위해 프로그래머블 셰이딩 GPU를 발명해 이것이 훗날 CUDA가 됐으며, 다시 협력해 GPU 슈퍼컴퓨터를 Azure에 올려 OpenAI의 GPT 학습을 도왔다. 이제 함께 개인 AI 에이전트 시대에 맞춰 Windows를 재구성하고 있으며, 4년에 걸쳐 양측이 수천 엔지니어-년을 투입했다. NVDA, MSFT 강세.
text:
Awesome day, @satyanadella! 

Windows sparked a platform shift that created a new industry for NVIDIA. Then we invented programmable shading GPUs for DirectX, which led to CUDA. 

Then we partnered to bring GPU supercomputers to Azure, which helped OpenAI train GPT. That collaboration inspired us to reinvent Windows for the age of personal agents.

4 years. Thousands of engineering years between us.

So proud of what we built together.

name: The Kobeissi Letter

ticker_notes.AVGO: 屬 AI 十大，佔美股市值紀錄 42%
ticker_notes.AMD: 屬 AI 十大，集中度高於網路泡沫 41%
ticker_notes.MU: 屬 AI 十大，比率自 2022 低點翻倍

zh_summary: KobeissiLetter 表示「AI 十大」市值佔美股總市值創新高 42%，包括七巨頭加上 Broadcom、AMD、Micron，比率自 2022 年熊市低點翻倍有餘。附美銀圖表比較：2000 年網路泡沫 TMT 高峰 41%、1970 年代 Nifty Fifty 40%、1980 年代日本泡沫 44%，只有 1900 年代鐵路股達到 63%。他表示大型科技股的主導程度非比尋常。AVGO、AMD、MU 中性。
ko_summary: KobeissiLetter는 "AI 톱10"의 시가총액이 미국 주식 전체 시가총액의 42%로 사상 최고를 기록했다고 했다. 매그니피센트 7에 Broadcom, AMD, Micron을 더한 것으로, 이 비율은 2022년 약세장 저점 이후 두 배 넘게 늘었다. 첨부한 BofA 차트 비교: 2000년 닷컴 버블 TMT 정점 41%, 1970년대 Nifty Fifty 40%, 1980년대 일본 버블 44%이며, 1900년대 철도주만 63%에 달했다. 대형 기술주의 지배력이 이례적이라고 했다. AVGO, AMD, MU 중립.
text:
BREAKING: The "AI Big 10" now accounts for a record 42% of US stock market cap.

This includes Magnificent 7 stocks as well as Broadcom, $AVGO, AMD, $AMD, and Micron, $MU.

This figure has more than doubled since the 2022 bear market low.

By comparison, during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble, the Technology, Media & Telecom (TMT) sector peaked at 41%, while the Nifty Fifty peaked at 40% in the 1970s.

Furthermore, Japan’s equity market bubble in the 1980s peaked at 44%.

In the past, only railroad stocks have significantly exceeded this concentration, accounting for 63% of US market cap at their highest point in the 1900s.

The dominance of Big Tech is extraordinary.
